answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The horizon multiplier is published, charged in haven, and wander lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 2885 identities would post 3733 proofs and burn roughly 64 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
